findings.summary: The approved spec's dd-acceptance gate is red: `npm test` exited 1 with {failed:2, passed:791, total:793} per the implement verification record, and .dev-dispatch/run-config.json lists that same command unscoped as an acceptance_command. No artifact identifies the two failing tests or establishes that they are pre-existing on the frozen base c76594d5f9e45a557b56044d585419a30a3113a8, so the change is not demonstrated to pass its own acceptance gate. (Read-only inspection found no plausible C1 causation -- no test enumerates the new root deploy/ directory, and the whole-src scans in mineru.test.ts and d1-deploy-config.test.ts E2 are unaffected by src/preflight.ts and src/preflight-entry.ts -- but causation cannot be excluded without identifying the failures.)

The Continuous review's dismissal of the red acceptance gate rests on a false premise. Its second finding claims "run-config.json scopes C1 acceptance test command to test/c1-preflight.test.ts"; .dev-dispatch/run-config.json contains no such scoping -- acceptance_commands is [["npm","ci"],["npm","run","typecheck"],["npm","test"],["npm","run","smoke:cas"]], with npm test unscoped. The only recorded justification for accepting exit_code 1 is therefore unsupported.

Provenance metadata is inconsistent: the committed implement handoff records work_head_commit=447acede49334c780ae728fdf3d7de3a1bae7691, while the dispatch attempt context states the product commit (work_head_commit) is ed5c82d94b830079a2efe17dbf1b3b061ea1993a. Non-blocking and consistent with a metadata-only seal stacked on the product commit, but the two records do not agree on the same SHA.

Review-coverage limitation, not a defect in the change: as a read-only reviewer restricted to file inspection I could not execute the prescribed mechanical check `git diff --exit-code ed5c82d9 583d6e7f -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'`. By direct inspection of the worktree at 583d6e7f I observed the complete C1 product implementation intact and found no product file bearing evidence of alteration by the review materialization seal; the deterministic verdict seal remains the authoritative independent check of the actual Git HEAD.
